text:
Hail, illustrious banner of Castile,

that waves today upon the walls of Tétouan

and sends to the Cuban Antilles

reflections of Spain's glories!

The crescent, which bows before you,

now recalls how, amid turbulent waves,

to the deep dread of Hagar's descendants,

it sank when Lepanto's star arose.


And those Moors, a disgrace to Europe,

who forgot the roar of your lions,

today, beneath the harsh blow that chastens them,

conjure fierce visions in their fear.

In the bloody light of seven centuries

they think they see, rising amid coats of arms,

with their turbans spread beneath their feet,

the shades of El Cid, Alfonso, and Guzmán.


Oh yes! Those august names go with you

and fight for you; the rays of their glory

flash in your folds, as they shine

throughout Spanish history.

May they forever triumph as symbols

of honor and victory, while civilization

proudly watches Tétouan welcome you today,

and Tangier tomorrow!

translation.title: To the Castilian Banner
